name: Cloud9 x JetBrains: Sky's The Limit Hackathon 2026
sponsor: Cloud9 (esports org) + JetBrains; managed by Devpost

prizes.per_category: Winner $6,000 cash + paid GDC trip + 1yr JetBrains All Products Pack + $100 Cloud9 gift card; Runner-up $2,000 cash + JetBrains sub
prizes.bonus: Best AI-Powered Workflow Story (amount not captured - gap)

eligibility.age: Above legal age of majority in country of residence
eligibility.countries: All except standard exceptions; rules name Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, US-sanctioned territories
eligibility.teams: Individuals, teams, and organizations all allowed

judging.criterion: Technological Implementation (thoroughness/skill of JetBrains tool use; working non-trivial implementation)
Potential Impact (credible case for a real audience)

judging_note: Official rules: Stage One pass/fail (theme fit + reasonable application of required JetBrains tools), Stage Two equally weighted 5 criteria (0.2 each, verbatim 'equally weighted criteria').
requirements: Build or significantly update a working project using at least one JetBrains tool (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, DataGrip, JetBrains Air, or AI Coding Agent Junie); registrants get free All Products Pack + AI Ultimate codes while supplies last

Enter one category: (1) VALORANT/Game Changers tactical scouting, utility placement & operator profiler; (2) League of Legends macro scouting & draft management; (3) event mini game playable at a Cloud9 booth (Rider recommended)
Project new, or if pre-existing significantly updated after Nov 17, 2026 (UX-changing updates only)
Public open-source repo (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) with detectable license, all source/assets/run instructions; commit .idea/.junie/.air folder as tool-use evidence
Text description explaining features and demonstrating JetBrains tool use
Working demo URL (web) or judge-accessible build with install instructions
Demo video <3 minutes, publicly visible on YouTube, showing the project running on its target device
Methodology write-up (approach + how the tool solves the category problem)
Original work, solely owned by entrant; open source OK if you build on top of it
GRID official esports data available but optional for every category
Riot-title-inspired projects must follow Riot developer policies; games must use original names/artwork/assets, not recreate Riot content
bans: No third-party trademarks, copyrighted music, or material in the video without permission
No projects developed with financial/preferential support from sponsor/promotion entities
No recreating Riot Games content (original names/assets required in games)
Residents of named excluded regions ineligible (Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, sanctioned countries)
No required cloud/paid LLM API anywhere in the rules - app inference may be fully local (fits local vLLM constraint)
competition_level: 245 participants (very low vs 1,000-16,000 at other live AI hackathons)
gaps: Bonus prize dollar amount not extracted
Sponsor-employee exclusion clause not explicitly seen in fetched rules text (Devpost standard exceptions likely apply) - re-read full rules before submitting
Operator's country of residence unknown - verify not in excluded-territory list
